title: The Hollow of the Glass Steppe
premise: Jonah Blackwood has hidden her gift for twelve years, selling harmless charms in the city of Vell, where magic was outlawed after the king's coronation. When the crown's witch-hunters begin burning the gifted out of the slums, Jonah flees into the Glass Steppe — a haunted plain where memories pool like water — pursued by Inquisitor Serane, who wears a stolen face. There Jonah learns the truth: the king never outlawed magic; the thing wearing his crown did, feeding on the fear and forgotten pasts of an entire kingdom. To save Vell, Jonah must cross the Steppe to the Hollow at its heart, unbind the king from his parasite, and choose between reclaiming her own stolen childhood memories or using them as the key that frees him.
about_author: Ansel Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters from people who had lost their memories to illness. They write fantasy about what power costs the powerless, and live near a salt marsh with two opinionated cats.

chapters.title: Charms for the Fearful
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She sells a luck-knot to a dockworker and hides her gift from a neighbor's prying eyes, establishing her careful double life in Vell. When royal criers announce a bounty on the gifted, her oldest customer is dragged away by witch-hunters. The emotional beat: guilt — she could have warned him, and didn't.

chapters.title: The Face That Isn't Hers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Inquisitor Serane arrives at Jonah's tenement wearing the face of her dead mentor, Maren. Recognizing the theft, Jonah burns her shop and flees through the sewers as hunters close in. The beat: terror sharpening into rage — they took Maren's face, and now they'll take everything.

chapters.title: Out Onto the Glass
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Beyond the city walls lies the Glass Steppe, where the ground mirrors the sky and lost memories shimmer in shallow pools. Jonah drinks one by accident and relives a fragment of a stranger's wedding. The beat: uneasy wonder — this terrible place might be the only place her gift can breathe.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Forgot His Name
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She rescues Tam, a feral child hollowed out by the Steppe, who remembers nothing but how to run. Caring for him cracks open her loneliness; teaching him small charms rekindles her joy in magic. The beat: tentative belonging — she hasn't been needed in twelve years.

chapters.title: What the Pools Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Serane hunting across the Steppe, glimpses of her own erased past inside the pools. She serves the crown willingly but cannot remember why she volunteered. The beat: dread — even the hunter is prey to whatever sits on the throne.

chapters.title: The Pilgrim at the Waystone
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At a waystone shrine she meets Ovid, a disgraced court magician exiled years ago, who reveals the truth of the Hollow: the king made a bargain at his coronation, and the thing he bound himself to rewrote the kingdom's memory of it. The beat: horrified clarity — the ban on magic was the parasite's feeding mechanism.

chapters.title: Serane's Hunt
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. She corners Jonah's group at dusk; Tam is captured, and Ovid dies buying their escape, his last spell erasing Serane's orders from her mind for one crucial hour. The beat: grief and fury — Jonah loses a friend and gains a deadline, because the hour will end.

chapters.title: Into the Hollow
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She trades her most precious memory — the day Maren first called her talented — to buy passage past the Steppe's guardian into the Hollow beneath the palace. Inside, she finds the king: old, half-dissolved, still fighting. The beat: sacrifice — she pays in the currency of self.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Split POV climax. Jonah begins the unbinding as Serane, freed by Ovid's erasure, turns against the parasite that stole her face and purpose. The creature offers Jonah her memories back if she abandons the king. The beat: the choice — she refuses, speaks the unbinding through tears, and the crown shatters.

chapters.title: A Kingdom That Remembers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Magic is decriminalized; the king, frail and grateful, offers her a court position she declines. She opens a school in Vell with Tam and a pardoned Serane, and plants a garden over her burned shop. The beat: quiet belonging — she gave up a memory of being chosen, and built a life where she chooses herself.
